messages:
Maya Chen: Quick idea — instead of the ad-hoc admit script, we make the intake an explicit state orchestra (state machine) + a cheap synthetic smoke bench step. goal: deterministic retry logic, better observability, cheaper fast-fail for obviously incompatible models.
Tony Alvarez: Love the idea. sketch a small state diagram? also worried synthetic benches might still spike infra cost if we run them for every model.
Maya Chen: Agreed, sampling + budget caps. rough states below (pseudo-yaml):
```
states:
  - queued
  - preflight_sanity
  - synthetic_smoke (fast latency/cost check)
  - interface_compat_check
  - fallback_full_bench (triggered on mismatch or periodic)
  - accepted
  - rejected
  - manual_review
transitions:
  queued -> preflight_sanity
  preflight_sanity -> synthetic_smoke | rejected
  synthetic_smoke -> interface_compat_check | manual_review
  interface_compat_check -> accepted | fallback_full_bench
  fallback_full_bench -> accepted | rejected
```
Ashok Patel: Nice. A couple notes:
- synthetic_smoke should reuse tiny golden prompts and fixed kv/cache seeds to keep variance low.
- cap synthetic to N tokens / model per day for cost control.
- bench artifacts must be small JSON bundles + model fingerprint.
Samira Khan: How do we wire metrics/alerts? want: admit.state gauge, admit.duration histogram, admit.fail_reason tag, sampled qualitative score.
Tony Alvarez: +1. also expose admit.run_id to the Console so users can click through artifact (benchbot://run/abcd).
Maya Chen: Implementation notes:
- controller service runs state machine (idempotent transitions), backed by datastore row per-model.
- worker pool consumes queued tasks, runs synthetic runner in sandboxed infra (cpu or cheap gpu).
- benchbot uploads artifacts to S3 and posts a short summary back to the thread.
- decision made by deterministic rule set + optional ML heuristic for false positive suppression.
Ashok Patel: Concern: cache-warming — some models only show perf once kv cache is warmed. synthetic_smoke must include a warmup phase or we risk false negatives. Proposed: run 10 warmup sequences + 5 measurement sequences.
Maya Chen: Good call. Marking warmup as configurable per-model class. Default: 5 warmup / 5 measure.
Samira Khan: Alerts: create an SLO for admit latency (p95 < 30m for light admits, < 6h if full bench), and a cost budget alert (daily synthetic token spend > $X triggers review).
Tony Alvarez: For compatibility checks, we should compute a deterministic fingerprint (api shape + tokenizer hash + param-shard-hash) and compare against known supported shapes. if unknown -> manual_review or fallback_full_bench.
benchbot: run 1704123456-1 started: model=mike-transformer-3 quant=8 warmup=5 measure=5
benchbot: run 1704123456-1 results uploaded -> s3://redwood-admit/runs/1704123456-1.json (latency_p50=38ms, p95=120ms, token_cost_est=0.003USD)
Tony Alvarez: Can we surface token_cost_est to the billing team early so Dedicated customers can opt-out of expensive automatic full benches?
Maya Chen: yes — add a cost_estimation step after synthetic_smoke. if over threshold, require opt-in for full_bench.
Ashok Patel: Also: versioned policies. policies/v1.json should encode thresholds per-class (llama-like vs encoder-only).
Samira Khan: UX: Console should show admit timeline (states + durations) and link to artifacts, plus a waveform of sample latencies. This will help SRE triage.
Maya Chen: Proposed rollout: feature-flag the orchestra, route 5% new models through new flow, compare final decisions vs existing script for 2 weeks.
Tony Alvarez: Add a circuit breaker: if synthetic_smoke failure rate > 10% in the last 24h we reduce sampling and route to manual_review to avoid noisy automated rejections.
Maya Chen: Action items: I will draft a concise RFC with state-machine contract + small POC plan. volunteers for POC: @Ashok, @Tony (you in?).
Ashok Patel: I'm in. happy to pair on the worker harness + artifact schema.
Tony Alvarez: I can take controller + telemetry wiring.
Samira Khan: I'll draft metric names and alert rules.
Maya Chen: Sweet. I'll have an RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. if no objections, we'll spin up a tiny PoC repo and an internal runspace. :thumbsup:
